questions.question: The objects which repeats its motion after some time is called _________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**periodic motion.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A motion that repeats itself after a set amount of time is called** periodic motion**.
 
• When a body repeatedly moves along a certain path over a predetermined amount of time, it is said to be exhibiting periodic motion.
 
• The term "**time period**" refers to the interval of time after which the body's motion is repeated.
 
• **Examples **of periodic motions:
 
 
• earth’s rotation around the sun
 
• motions of the hands of a clock
 
 
 
• When a body moves in a** non-periodic** manner, it doesn't repeat the same motion after a set amount of time.
 
 
• A bouncing ball, for instance, moves in a non-periodic manner.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rectilinear motion or linear motion** is a type of motion that only moves in one direction or on one axis.

 
 
• Every parameter connected to motion is pointed in the same direction.
 
• Consequently, the motion is sometimes referred to as **one-dimensional motion.**
 
• **Examples**:
 
 
• soldiers walking on the ground or marching during the event.
 
• arrow fired by an archer
 
• a car moving on a road
 
• a person jogging in park
 
 
 
 
 
• ​An object moving while rotating in a circle is referred to as being in **circular motion.**
 
 
• There are two types of circular motion: uniform and non-uniform.
 
• The angular rate of rotation and speed will remain constant in uniform circular motion, whereas the rate of rotation will fluctuate in non-uniform motion.
 
• Common **examples **of circular motion:
 
 
• rotating ceiling fan
 
• moving car’s wheel
 
• blades of windmill
 
• Merry-Go-Round
 
 
 
 
 
• When the object rotates for half circle and comes back, this is called **semi-circular motion**.

questions.question: Which among the following is a famous festival of Maharashtra, India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gudi Padva.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Hindu New Year**, known in **Maharashtra **as **Gudi Padwa,** in** Andhra Pradesh and Telangana** as **Ugadi**, and in **other parts of India** as **Chaitra Navratri.**
 
• Gudi Padwa is a major festival in Maharashtra, but it is also celebrated in Goa, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and some parts of Gujarat and Rajasthan.
 
• The event is held on the** first day of Chaitra month,** which is the first month in the Hindu Panchangam calendar, and often takes place in** March or Apri**l.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The largest celebration in the Indian state of **Kerala **is **Onam**.

 
 
• The Onam Festival commemorates the return of the mythical **King Mahabali** and takes place during the Malayali month of Chingam (Aug–Sep).
 
• The** ten-day Onam Carnival** showcases the finest aspects of Keralan customs and culture.
 
• Kerala's harvest festival, Onam, is known for its elaborately decorated **Pookalam**, delicious **Onasadya**, magnificent **Snake Boat Race**, and unique **Kaikottikali dance**, among other amazing events.
 
 
 
• One of the most important festivals in India is **Chhath Puja.**
 
 
• The majority of **Bihar**, **Uttar Pradesh**, and some **regions of Nepal** commemorate this event.
 
• On the **sixth day** of the month of **Kartika**, the festival begins.
 
• The **four-day celebration** is devoted to **worshiping the Sun** in order to ask for his blessing and to offer prayers for the family's continued prosperity and health.
 
• On this auspicious day, people pray to Lord Sun and immerse themselves in the Ganga's sacred waters.
 
• The day celebrates the benevolent act of Lord Sun and his wife for granting this beautiful life on the earth

questions.question: Who established the Ramakrishna Mission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Vivekananda**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Swami Vivekananda was born on **12th January**, 1863 in **Calcutta **(now Kolkata). He died in 1902.
 
• His original name was Narendranath Datta. 
 
• He was an Indian Hindu monk, philosopher, author, religious teacher, thinker, and patriot.
 
• He was the **founder **of the Ramkrishna Mission.
 
• He introduced the Indian philosophies of Vedanta and Yoga to the world.
 
• In 1893 he gave his famous speech to the World's Parliament of Religions also known as the Chicago speech.
 
• In **1984 **Government decided to celebrate **12th January as National Youth Day.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Informatio__**

 
• **Muni Tarun Sagar** was an Indian **Digambara monk**.

 
 
• Because of their tendency to be frank in their criticism of accepted beliefs and behaviors, his **lectures **are known as **Kadve Pravachan**, or biting talks. His talks have been collected and made available as part of the Kadve Pravachan book series.
 
• In contrast to the bulk of other Digambar Jain monks, he frequently had a predominantly non-Jains audience.
 
• He frequently discussed family and societal concerns in his talks.
 
 
 
• **Gaur Gopal Das** is an Indian monk, lifestyle coach, motivational speaker and former electrical engineer.
 
 
• He is a member of the **International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON).**
 
 
 
• **Jambuvijaya**, also called **Muni Jambuvijayji Maharajsaheb**, was a monk from the **Svetambara sect of Jainism** who belonged to the **Tapa Gaccha order**.
 
 
• His groundbreaking work in the fields of ancient text and Jain Agamas investigation, cataloging, and translation was well known.
 
• He was in charge of unearthing and disseminating several old Jains manuscripts that were hidden away in various abandoned Jain jnana bhandaras (ancient Jain libraries).
 
• He was **Muni Punyavijay's** pupil.

questions.question: In which Indian movement, were the issues faced by indigo planters, first brought to light in 1917?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Champaran Satyagraha.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The issues faced by** indigo planters**, first brought to light in **1917 **in **Champaran Satyagraha**.
 
• Champaran is a district in the state of Bihar, India.
 
• In 1917, the peasants of Champaran were forced to cultivate indigo by the British landlords, which resulted in their exploitation and oppression.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi,** who was then a young lawyer, was invited by a local leader to investigate the matter.
 
• He stayed in Champaran for several months and organized a successful Satyagraha movement against the British landlords.
 
• Here, for the first time in India, Gandhi used Civil Disobedience as tool for satyagraha.
 
• The Tinkathia system was prevalent in Champaran district of Bihar during the British Raj.
 
 
• It was a system of forced cultivation of indigo on a portion of the farmer's land in exchange for rent-free land for personal cultivation.
 
• The farmers of Champaran were compelled to grow indigo on 3/20th of their land (i.e. three kathas per beegha) by the British planters who had leased the land from the local landlords.

questions.question: What did the medieval term "Raqs" mean?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dancing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The medieval term "**Raqs**" means **belly dancing**.
 
• It features movements of the hips and torso.
 
• With the migration of the **Gypsy tribes**, it began more than 5000 years ago in **Egypt **and spread throughout the Middle East.
 
• Eventually, they arrived in **Europe**, the birthplace of the well-known Gypsy dance, **Flamenco**.
 
• **Belly dancing** and modern **flamenco **share a lot of **similarities**.
 
• It originated from a religious dance performed as a **fertility ritual** by priestesses and is a dance that was **part of the birthing rite **and helped women get ready for labor.
 
• It was inspired by a social dance from ancient **Egypt**.

questions.question: The summer months experience ________ in the northern part of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**falling air pressure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **summer months** experience **falling air pressure** in the northern part of India.
 
• **May to mid-March** is regarded as the **summer season**.
 
• The main characteristics of this season are **high temperatures** and** low humidity.**
 
• The hot weather season is also known as the pre-monsoon season. Because the sun seems to straddle the equator and the Tropic of Cancer, there is a large range in sun insolation.
 
• As per the Hindu calendar, this season mainly occurs in **Jyeshta **and **Aashaadha**.
 
• The **mean temperature** stays approximately at **38 degrees Celsius**.
 
• This is the season with the **longest days** and the **shortest nights.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Winter Season** runs from the middle of **December to the middle of March.**

 
 
• It experience **decreasing temperature **and** rising air pressure** in the northern part of India.
 
• It appears that the **sun is traveling south of the equator**. Clear skies, comfortable temperatures, mild trade winds from the northeast, low humidity, and a wide range of temperatures characterize this season.
 
• The country's interior has exceptionally large variations in temperature throughout the day, especially in the winter.
 
 
 
• In India, the months of **June through September **are referred to as the **Monsoon or Rainy Season**.
 
 
• It is the season of heavy rain in northern part of India.
 
• The northwest plains have experienced a notable** rise in temperature **in May, which has exacerbated the **low-pressure system** there.
 
 
• They get powerful enough by early June to attract Southern Hemisphere-native trade winds from the Indian Ocean.
 
• These** southeast trade winds** cross the equator and then go over the **Arabian Sea **and the** Bay of Bengal** before becoming entangled in the airflow over India.
 
• They bring a plenty of moisture with them as they traverse the **warm equatorial currents**.
 
• They move southwestward after reaching the equator. The **southwest monsoon** is named as a result.

questions.question: Who among the following is a sitar maestro of global acclaim?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shahid Parvez Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indian classical **sitar maestro** **Ustad Shahid Parvez Khan**, also known as Shahid Parvez, was born on October 14, 1954, into the Imdadkhani gharana.
 
• As the principal exponent of the **Etawah Gharana**, he represents the seventh generation.
 
• He is highly regarded, particularly for the vocal phrasing and caliber of his** "Gayaki Ang" (Singing branch/limb) raga** improvisations.
 
• He was awarded Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2006 and **Padma Shri Award in 2012**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Girija Devi** was an Indian **classical vocalist** from the** Seniya and Banaras gharanas**, who lived from **8 May 1929** until 24 October 2017.

 
 
• She promoted thumri and raised awareness of it by performing classical and light classical music.
 
• Because of her influence on the genre, she was crowned the "**Queen of Thumri.**" 
 
• She received **Padma Shri **(1972), **Padma Bhushan** (1989), Padma Vibhushan (2016)[10], Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1977), Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (2010) and many other notable awards.
 
 
 
• Born on July 27, 1950, **Vishwa Mohan Bhatt**, often known as V. M. Bhatt, is an instrumentalist in Hindustani classical music who **plays the Mohan veena (slide guitar)**.
 
 
• He was awarded **1993 Grammy Award (Best World Music Album) – A Meeting by the River(With Ry Cooder)**, Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1998, Padma, Shri in 2002, Padma Bhushan in 2017.
 
 
 
• Bismillah Khan was an Indian musician credited with popularizing the **shehnai**, a reeded woodwind instrument. 
 
 
• He was born on March 21, 1916, into a family of traditional Muslim musicians at the town of Dumraon (Buxar, Bihar) in British India.
 
• He became the first Indian to be invited to **perform **at the prestigious** Lincoln Centre Hall in the United States of America**.
 
• He also took part in the World Exposition in Montreal, the Cannes Art Festival, and in the Osaka Trade Fair.
 
• So well known did he become internationally that an auditorium in Teheran was named after him — Tahar Mosiquee Ustaad Bismillah Khan.
 
• National awards like the **Padma Shri** in 1961, the Padma Bhushan in 1968, and the Padma Vibhushan in 1980 were conferred on him.
 
• In 2001, He was awarded India’s highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna.

questions.question: Which among the following bills passed in Parliament in 2022 replaced the Identification of Prisoners Act, 1920?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Criminal Procedure (Identification) Bill**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Criminal Procedure (Identification) Bill** passed in Parliament in **2022**.
 
• It takes the place of the **Identification of Prisoners Act, 1920**, a statute from the colonial era that permits police to measure individuals who are accused, detained, or awaiting trial in criminal situations.
 
• It gives the police legal permission to collect bodily and biological samples from both criminal suspects and prisoners.
 
• The **Law Commission of India's 87th Report **reviewed this statute in **1980 **and made several recommendations for changes. These recommendations were added in the bill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• On December 3, 2021, the **Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) (Amendment) Bill, 2021 **was presented to the Lok Sabha. 

 
 
• The** Central Vigilance Commission (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021** is superseded by it. 
 
• The **CVC Act of 2003** is intended to be amended by the bill. A Central Vigilance Commission is to be established in accordance with the 2003 Act to **investigate claims of offenses against the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.** 
 
 
 
• On December 20, 2021, the **Election Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2021 **was presented to the Lok Sabha. 
 
 
• In order to achieve specific electoral reforms, the Bill **alters **the **Representation of the People Acts of 1950 and 1951**. 
 
• The 1950 Act specifies voter criteria, electoral roll compilation, seat distribution, and boundary delimitation for elections. 
 
• The 1951 Act governs election administration, as well as election-related offenses and disputes.
 
 
 
• The **Farm Laws Repeal Bill, 2021** was introduced in Lok Sabha on November 29, 2021 **by **the Minister of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, **Mr. Narendra Singh Tomar**.
 
 
• The** three agriculture laws** that Parliament passed in September 2020 are repealed by the Bill. 
 
• These include the **Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2020**, the** Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act, 2020**, and the** Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020**. 
 
• These laws were passed in order to:
 
 
• (i) establish a legal framework for contract farming;
 
• (ii) make it easier for farmers to trade their produce without obstacles outside of the markets that are alerted by the various state Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee (APMC) laws; and
 
• (iii) control the supply of specific foods (like cereals, pulses, and onions) only in extreme cases, like famine, war, or sharp price increases.

questions.question: Fishes have ________ chambers of the heart.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **heart **of a **fish **has **two chambers**.
 
• There is only** one ventricle** and **one atrium** in the heart.
 
• The ventricle is in charge of pumping blood into the atrium.
 
• Fish likewise have** unidirectional flow**, or a **single circulation** in a single direction.
 
• A** fish’s heart is also known as** a **venous heart** because it is filled with deoxygenated blood.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Number of chambers of the heart in different species:
 
• 
 
 
 

 **Species**

questions.question: The kingdoms of Chola, Chera and Pandyas belong to which period in the ancient India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sangam Period**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Sangam Age, sometimes referred to as the Tamil Sangam period, was an important period in South India's history. It is generally believed that the Sangam era occurred between 300 BCE and 300 CE.
 
• Three dynasties—the Chera, Chola, and Pandyas—ruled the Tamil nation during the Sangam Period. They were Muvendar, jointly as well.
 
• For administrative convenience, the kingdom was split into the following divisions: Mandalam (territory), Nadu (province), Ur (town), Perur (large village), and Sirur (small village).
 
• More terms used in sangam age:
 
 
• Karai: Land tax 
 
• Ulgu: Customs duties
 
• Iravu: Forced gift/extra demand 
 
• Irai: Tribute paid by feudatories 
 
• Variyar: Tax collector
 
• Vanigar: Traders and Merchants
 
• Arasar: Ruling Class
 
• Vellalars: Dominant Agricultural caste
 
• Uzhavars: Middle-class Agricultural caste
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
Mauryan Period:

 
 
• Chandragupta Maurya was the founder of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• He is referred to in Greek sources as Sandrokottos.
 
• In 321 BC, he defeated Dhana Nanda and took the throne with the aid of a politically astute and clever Brahmin named Kautilya.
 
• Megasthenes served as the Greek representative in the court of Chandragupta.
 
• He led an expansionist policy that subjugated nearly all of modern-day India, except a few isolated areas in the far south and Kalinga.
 
• Bindusara is the second Mauryan Empire ruler.
 
• 297–273 BC was his rule period.
 
• He was also called Amitraghata (Slayer of foes).
 
• Ashoka mentions in his inscription that he conquered Kalinga after becoming the king for eight years.
 
• Kalinga was a region located in present-day Odisha and parts of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Ashoka established Ujjain and Takshashila (later Taxila) as the regional capitals of his kingdom.
 
 
 
• **Mahajanapada period:**
 
 
• **​**In **Jambudipa (Bharatvarsha)**, there were **sixteen **republics of significant size and authority known as **"Solasa Mahajanapada**," according to the **Buddhist **canonical scripture** Anguttara Nikaya**.
 
• The sixteen Mahajanapadas belonged to either a **republican or monarchical political structure**.
 
• The republics were located in present-day Punjab in northwest India and along the foothills of the Himalayas, while the monarchies were primarily located in the Gangetic Plains.
 
• They existed from the** 6th to 4th century BCE**.

questions.question: The Narmada river rises in the Amarkantak hills situated in which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amarkantak Hills** is situated in Anuppur district of the state of **Madhya Pradesh** at an altitude of 1065m at the** meeting place of the Vindhya and Satpura** mountain ranges.
 
• The mighty **Narmada river** as well the **Son**, the **Mahanadi**, and **Arnadoh **which is a major **tributary of the Godavari** all **arise in the Amarkantak plateau**.
 
• There are over **24 temples** in and around Amarkantak, including the **Devi Sati temple** and the historic temple devoted to the **Goddess Narmada.**
 
• The **Trimukhi temple**, the oldest in Amarkantak, is devoted to **Lord Shiva**. Between 1042-1122 AD,** Karan Chendi,** the ruler, constructed it.
 
• Distinguished instances of **Kalchuri art** and skill can be seen in the **Machendranathh** at the **Pataleshwar temple.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Narmada River,** located in central India, has long served as a vital conduit between the Ganges River valley and the **Arabian Sea**.

 
 
• The **Greek **geographer Ptolemy named the river **Namade **in the second century CE.
 
 
 
• The river is **1,312 km long,** of which 1079 km are in Madhya Pradesh. The remaining 35 km of the river's length defines the common boundary between Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, and the remaining 39 km between Maharashtra and Gujarat.
 
• Its principal **tributaries **are the **Burhner**, the **Halon**, the Heran, the Banjar, the **Dudhi**, the Shakkar, the **Tawa**, the **Barna **,the **Kolar**, the Ganjal, the Beda, the Goi, and the **Orsang**.
 
• Among the **projects **under construction in the basin, **Sardar Sarovar**, **Indira Sagar**, Bargi and **Omkareshwar** are the most important.

questions.question: The first urban settlement to reach a population of one million was _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**London.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first urban settlement to reach a population of one million** was the city of **London **by around. A.D. **1810**.
 
• It was followed by **Paris **in **1850**, **New York** in **1860**, and by 1950 there were around 80 such cities.
 
• The rate of increase in the number of million cities has been three-fold in every three decades – around 160 in 1975 to around 438 in 2005.
 
• **London **is the city and **capital **of the **United Kingdom**.
 
 
• It is located 50 miles (80 km) upstream from the **River Thames'**s estuary on the **North Sea**, in southeast **England**.
 
• In the past, London originated from three main locations: the walled community established by the Romans in the first century CE on the banks of the Thames, now called the City of London, "**the Square Mile**," or simply "**the City**"; the suburb of Southwark, which is located across the bridge on the lower gravels of the south bank; and the City of Westminster, which is located one mile upstream on a large southward bend of the river.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In his seminal essay **"Cities as systems within systems of cities,"** **Brian J.L. Berry **(1964) established the** idea of the urban system**.

 
 
• The concept of urban hierarchy takes into account the differences in population sizes and economic roles among** metropolitan areas**.
 
• The primary focus of the examination of urban hierarchy is the ranking of cities according to many factors, including retail sales, industrial worker count, population size, and economic power.
 
• Rapid urbanization is a relatively new development. Few communities had populations of more than a few thousand people up until recently.
 
• The city of **London **became the **first urban community to have a million residents by the year 1810**. 
 
 
 
• Any **city **with a** population of more than 10 million people**, including its suburbs, is referred to as a **Mega city** or **megalopolis**.
 
 
• **New York**, which had a population of roughly 12.5 million, was the** first to become a megacity by 1950**.

questions.question: Which Indian ministry introduced the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Bill, 2019?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Home Affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Bill, 2019** was **introduced **in Rajya Sabha on** August 5, 2019** by the **Minister of Home Affairs**, Mr.** Amit Shah**.
 
• The **Bill reorganises **the state of **Jammu and Kashmir** into:
 
 
• (i) the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir with a legislature, and
 
• (ii) the Union Territory of Ladakh without a legislature. 
 
 
 
• The** Union Territory of Ladakh** will comprise Kargil and Leh districts, and the **Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir** will comprise the remaining territories of the existing state of Jammu and Kashmir.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019:

 
 
• It was passed in **Rajya Sabha** on **5th August 2019** and then passed by the **Lok Sabha** on **6th August 2019** and it received the **president's assent** on **9th August 2019**.
 
• The Act also repealed Article 370, which had granted Jammu and Kashmir special status.
 
• On October 31, 2019, the day of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth, which is observed as National Unity Day, it came into force.
 
• Five Lok Sabha seats in Jammu and Kashmir were retained by the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, while one was transferred to the Union Territory of Ladakh.

questions.question: ______ are the vessels which carry carbon dioxide-rich blood back to the heart.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**veins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Veins **carry **carbon dioxide-rich or deoxygenated blood from all parts of the body back to the heart.**
 
• Your body has veins, which are blood vessels that **gather blood with low oxygen content** and return it to your heart.
 
 
• **Pulmonary veins** are an **exception **to this rule. These four veins, located between your heart and lungs, **carry oxygen-rich blood** from your lungs back to your heart.
 
 
 
• A component of your circulatory system are veins. To keep your blood flowing, they cooperate with your heart and other blood veins.
 
• The majority of your blood is stored in your veins. Your **veins actually contain around 75% of your blood.**
 
• Common **problems **with veins include **chronic venous insufficiency**, **deep vein thrombosis** and **varicose veins**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Your body uses **arteries**, which are a **component of the circulatory or cardiovascular system**, to **transport oxygen-rich blood from your heart to every cell in your body**.

 
 
• They are essential for the proper **distribution of hormones**, **nutrients**, and **oxygen **throughout your body.
 
• Because they carry nutrients to your body's cells and tissues, arteries help your body stay alive and healthy.
 
• 
 
There are **two varieties **of arteries:

 
 
• 
 
**Elastic**: Found near your heart, they have more elastic tissue than muscular arteries. **Aorta **and **pulmonary artery** are two examples.

 
 
• 
 
**Smooth (muscular) muscle** is more prevalent than elastic arteries in the muscle. **Brachial**, **radial**, and **femoral arteries** are a few examples.

 
 
 
 
 
 
• **Capillaries **are delicate blood vessels that exist throughout your body.
 
 
• They** transport blood, nutrients and oxygen to cells** in your organs and body systems.
 
• They are the **smallest blood vessels** in your vascular system. 
 
• They ​complete the circulatory system by **connecting arteries to veins**.
 
 
 
• The **basic building blocks of the brain** and **nervous system** are **neurons**, also known as **neurones or nerve cells**.
 
 
• Neurons are the cells that **receive sensory information** from the outside world, give motor commands to our muscles, and **convert and relay electrical signals** at each stage along the way.
 
• Their encounters, more than anything else, shape who we are as individuals.
 
• Nevertheless, there is interaction between our about 100 billion neurons and other cell types that are often referred to as **glia **(these may actually exceed neurons, but it's not truly known).

questions.question: Which among the following words were added to the Preamble in the 42nd amendment of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Socialist**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act 1976** brought about significant changes and additions to the Constitution, including the insertion of fundamental duties and the extension of emergency provisions.
 
• It ​is termed as "**Mini Constitution**".
 
• The **preamble **was **amended **by the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act in 1976**, in which three new words **Socialist**, **Secular**, and **Integrity **were **added**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Preamble **is called the introduction letter of the Indian Constitution.

 
 
• The preamble can be referred to as the preface which highlights the entire Constitution.
 
• It was adopted on 26 November 1949 by the Constituent Assembly and came into effect on 26 January 1950, celebrated as the Republic day in India.
 
 
 
• Important changes by 42nd Amendment of Indian Constitution 1976:

 
 

 Part of change
 Details
 
 

 Preamble
 'Sovereign Democratic Republic' was replaced by “Sovereign

 Socialist Secular Democratic Republic” and 'unity of the Nation' was replaced by “unity and

 integrity of the Nation”.
 
 

 Article 51A was added
 Introduced 10 fundamental duties of citizens.
 
 

 Judicial Powers of the High Court
 Reduced the judiciary review power of high courts.
 
 

 DPSPs (Directive Principles of State Policies)
 
 
Three new DPSPs (Directive Principles of State Policy) were added and one was amended:

 
1. Article 39 - To secure opportunities for the healthy development of children.

 
2. Article 39 A - To promote equal justice and to provide free legal aid to the poor.

 3. Article 43 A - To take steps to secure the participation of workers in the management of industries.

 4. Article 48 A - To protect and improve the environment and to safeguard forests and wildlife.

questions.question: Prayer halls in Buddhist architectural monuments were also known as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**chaitya grihas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chaitya Grihas** refers to a **shrine**, sanctuary, temple, or** prayer hall** in Buddhist architectural monuments.
 
• The majority of surviving early examples of chaitya are found in Indian rock-cut architecture.
 
• Chaityas **has a massive hall **with a tall vaulted ceiling and ornate sculptures at the entrance and pillars.
 
• The **Karle caves** are the **biggest Chaitya-Griha** of all the **Buddhist sites in India.**
 
• Numerous Chaityas display a stupa at the rear. Chaityas were carved as pillarless apsidal vault halls, **rectangular halls**, or **apsidal vault-roof halls**.
 
• **Ellora**, **Ajanta**, **Bhaja**, Bagh, **Karle**, Nasik, and **Kanheri **are some of the most beautiful Chaitya caves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
**Buddhism **and **Jainism **are the two main sources of inspiration for many Indian architectural styles.

 
 
• 
 
**Buddhist** advancements were as dynamic between the **sixth and the fifteenth century,** frequently collaborating closely with Hindu developments.

 
 
• 
 
There are Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain monuments in places like **Ellora**.

 
 
• 
 
**Bodhgaya **is the most important Buddhist site in India.

 
 
• 
 
Due to the fact that Bodhgaya is a pilgrimage place, it is where Siddhartha attained enlightenment and became the Buddha.

 
 
• 
 
The **Mahabodhi Temple** at Bodhgaya is a significant legacy of the brickwork from that era, even if the** Bodhi tree** is of utmost importance.

 
 
 
 
 
 
• **Stupas **: Typically solid and **bell-shaped**, stupas **contain **a **holy relic**—such as a Buddha's hair or teeth—as well as holy Buddhist texts or notable Buddha figures.
 
 
• **Buddha's symbol** is a **stupa**.
 
• The Buddhist stupas represent the Buddhist conception of the universe. 
 
• The most famous among these are **Sanchi**, **Bharhut **and **Amaravati**.
 
 
 
• **Viharas**: It was the name given to a **Buddhist monastery** in ancient India.
 
 
• Viharas were initially temporary homes for itinerant monks during the rainy season, but thanks to donations from affluent lay Buddhists, they eventually developed into **Buddhist educational institutions**.
 
• Early on, "Viharas" codified life. It is the subject of the **Vinaya Pitaka**, or "**basket of monastic discipline,**" which is a portion of the Pali canon.
 
• Numerous viharas can be found in typical big locations like the **Ajanta Caves**, Aurangabad Caves, **Karli Caves**, and **Kanheri Caves**.
 
 
 
• An **iwan **is a **rectangular hall **or room that has **one end completely open** and three walls surrounding it.
 
 
• Typically, it is vaulted. The **ceremonial entrance to the iwan** is known as the "**pishtaq**," which is a Persian word for a doorway that protrudes from a building's exterior and is typically embellished with geometric patterns, glazed tilework, and calligraphy bands.
 
• These are most commonly associated with** Islamic architecture**
